messages:
ada: heads-up — ran a 6h canary for redwood-m3-int8 (quantized build) against main redwood-m3-fp16. posting quick summary, flagging A/B and fallback decisions.

rj: thanks. short TL;DR first? :eyes:

ada: TL;DR — latency wins (p95 down ~35ms), cost per-token ~22% lower, but a small QA-accuracy regression on our high-sensitivity eval (~1.6% absolute). A/B pval ~0.03.

maria: can you paste the exact metrics and which eval sets?

ada: sure — key numbers: 
- eval set: hs-qa-320 (privacy-critical prompts)
- baseline acc: 87.3%
- int8 acc: 85.7%
- delta: -1.6pp (relative -1.83%)
- p95 lat baseline: 210ms
- p95 lat int8: 175ms
- median lat improv: ~18%
- tokens/sec +12%
- token cost delta: -22%

sachin: pval 0.03 is borderline for us. what's our current auto-fallback threshold?

ada: current auto-fallback in Dedicated is: trigger if (quality_drop >= 2.0pp) OR (pval < 0.01 AND quality_drop >= 1.0pp) OR (p95_latency > SLA + 50ms). That's config in rollout service.

maria: so this is below the 2pp hard threshold, but pval is not super strong either. does the regression concentrate on any categories?

ada: dug into confusion matrix. Most regressions are in multi-step reasoning where model now drops a supporting fact occasionally. Single-turn factual Qs are fine.

eve: can we run targeted shadow traffic with prompt tagging to see real-world impact on top customers?

ada: already ran a 100k shadow sample from canary window — aggregated conversion-like metrics show no detectable customer-visible degradation (CTR proxy unchanged). But hs-qa set is sensitive.

rj: i'm worried about long-tail failures. what if we promote and it drifts over larger distribution? any hysteresis plans?

maria: propose staged promotion: 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 48h with auto-eval at each step. if hs-qa delta > 1.2pp at any step OR overall pval < 0.02 then rollback. add cooldown 2h between steps.

ada: config snippet for proposal:
```
promotion_steps: [0.02, 0.10, 0.50]
step_interval: 48h
cooldown: 2h
auto_fallback_rules:
  - type: quality_delta
    metric: hs_qa_accuracy
    threshold_pp: 1.2
    comparison: decrease
  - type: pvalue_check
    metric: hs_qa_accuracy
    pvalue_threshold: 0.02
    min_delta_pp: 0.5
```

sachin: that seems reasonable. recommend also gating on hallucination_rate (we have a detector) — set threshold 0.8pp increase.

ada: added hallucination gate locally, re-run quick sim. when I apply that gate the canary fails at 10% step in ~45% of bootstrap samples.

rj: interesting — so if we keep conservative thresholds we probably won't promote automatically. Do we want to accept the tradeoff (latency/cost) vs manual rollout?

maria: product/customer impact call: for Hosted customers we can be more aggressive; for Dedicated/Private we should be conservative. Maybe auto-promote only in hosted with thresholds 1.6pp and pval 0.03, but require manual approval for Dedicated.

eve: agree. also add a shadow-compare stage where we compare embeddings similarity drift for content-moderation flows. that's another failure mode.

ada: notes from A/B buckets — short examples of failure: 
- prompt id 54211: chain-of-thought truncated, dropped source line -> incorrect step
- prompt id 54890: hallucinated a date in 2nd step (low confidence tokens)

rj: can we tune quantization (per-channel vs per-tensor) to regain some QA accuracy while keeping cost win?

ada: tested per-channel nf4 vs baseline nf4-per-tensor: per-channel recovers ~0.7pp acc (to 86.4) but increases cost delta to -15% (still good) and latency still ~-30ms p95. Looks promising.

maria: action items then:
- ada: run step promotion sim with new per-channel quant config + hallucination gate (due EOD)
- sachin: update rollout policy draft to split hosted vs dedicated thresholds (due tomorrow)
- eve: add shadow-compare job for embeddings drift and link to rollout dashboard (due this week)
- rj: schedule a short review with SE for high-sensitivity customers (tomorrow)

ada: also tagging deploy-bot — machine-checked canary logs are attached in the build:2101 run.

deploy-bot: build 2101 canary complete — artifacts: s3://redwood-prod/canaries/2101/; summary CSV: s3://redwood-prod/canaries/2101/summary.csv

maria: sounds good. if ada's per-channel run passes the 1.2pp + hallucination gate we can proceed with staged promotion in hosted only, manual for dedicated.

rj: +1. keep notes in the rollout ticket and let's not auto-promote until we see per-channel results. :thumbsup:

ada: will post a follow-up message with new numbers. thanks all.

sachin: thanks — FYI I bumped the rollback-alert to include slack @oncall if any auto-fallback triggers.

ada: perfect.

maria: filing a quick post-canary doc in the rollout ticket with the config and sample failures.

ada: done — ticket RD-8891 updated with artifacts and the proposed promotion policy.

rj: ok closing thread for now, reopen if new regressions show up. :shipit:
